dedupe_keys.name: nist distributed sensing of radio spectrum occupancy amid covid 19

description: This NIST dataset contains measurements of channel power and occupancy in the radio spectrum made during the COVID-19 pandemic. Measurements were taken at 13 residential telework sites of NIST staff and students after a rapid engineering development effort, followed by spot measurements at a local hospital, and continued where possible from late spring 2020 until autumn 2021. The targeted bands were cellular network bands below 1 GHz and unlicensed WLAN and WPAN bands at 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz. The data are released as time series of band power integrated over 4 MHz in 0.5 ms bins, denoised band power series, occupancy durations, histograms of band power readings and diagnostic network profiling data on PHY characteristics of cellular and WLAN signals, in 158 resources. Producer: NIST; the catalog was last updated on 20 April 2022. Coverage: US residential sites and one hospital, not a national survey. Access: TXT and GZIP downloads through the catalog with no login. Licence and cost: NIST open data licence, free. Caveats: a small number of sites during a period of unusual home working, so patterns may not generalise. Simulation uses: measured spectrum loading and occupancy patterns inform wireless capacity and demand models for residential broadband traffic shifts. Related record: the ITU frequency register for terrestrial services (data-itu-br-ific-terrestrial-services), which lists the assignments these measurements observe.
